bridge.credentialKey: Credential key for the current service
bridge.credentialKeyMissing: No service address yet, so there is no key to store under — enter one above first
bridge.egressHint: One way out for requests: the browser’s own fetch on the web, the host on the desktop. A browser is bound by its origin; another origin must allow it.
bridge.hintClient: These abilities come from the desktop shell; a browser has no host
bridge.hostHint: These come from the desktop shell: credential store, system integration, pickers, opening the browser. A browser has no host, so the buttons answer "no host".
bridge.serviceAddressHint: On the desktop the user types or picks it, and the host holds it (it survives restarts); the address is never baked into the artifact. The host checks an address before saving it, and the service document is still read by the application, the same way on both clients.

overview.title: Overview
requests.authzHint: A successful sign-in only means the credential is authenticated; whether a protected endpoint can be called still depends on the engine’s authorization policy. When the credential is sent and refused, the cell says authenticated but not authorized.
requests.listUsersHint: Fetch the user list and show the email of the first few; each email can sign in once.
requests.loginHint: Press Sign in on a row: how to sign in is the data layer's business (a host-held credential gets a token, otherwise the server sets a cookie).
requests.loginTestHint: These endpoints exist only on the development instance; a production engine does not register them. Press Sign in on a user row: how to sign in is the data layer's business.
requests.noEmailForLogin: This account has no email; test sign-in accepts email only
requests.scaffoldHint: The two public calls run for real; sign in through “Sign-in (test mode)” before pressing the protected pair, which explain any refusal by its code. Every request carries the current language and theme.
requests.statesHint: The four stages of one fetch: not started, in progress, done, failed — shown with the public GET.
